neighbours.label: 'which' (or 'allow for') introducing a clause about the effect or benefit that follows from the preceding cause
fire: Cutting prices attracted more shoppers, which pushed sales up by ten percent.
Cloud tools allow for quicker teamwork between distant offices.
Regular sleep strengthens memory, which makes learning much easier.
Solar panels lower the bill, which lets families save for college.
Remote work allows for more flexible schedules in most firms.
Good lighting reduces mistakes, which raises output in the factory.
Cheap flights allow for more frequent family visits abroad.
Early screening finds tumors sooner, which improves survival rates.
quiet: We stopped at the bakery, which was painted bright yellow.
She could not decide which coat to wear to the wedding.
The museum, which opened in 1920, sits near the river.
He asked which train goes to the coast after noon.
The letter, which was written in blue ink, had faded badly.
Tell me which of the two doors is locked at night.
Cheap flights are listed on the board by the gate.
The cabin, which smelled of pine, had one small window.

notes: triage: context. probe: causal which/allow for 0.22-0.24; descriptive which 0.03. Expect borderline.
